newsitem.title: NORWAY: Esso delays Balder oil start from September.
newsitem.headline: Esso delays Balder oil start from September.

text.p: Esso Norge said on Wednesday start up of the Balder oilfield in the North Sea would be delayed from September as planned, but it could not give a new date for the field to come onstream.
The 4.7 billion crown Balder project was originally scheduled to begin operations between the end of 1996 and the beginning of the second quarter 1997.
In December Esso said the project would be postponed by eight to 10 weeks while work was carried out on the floating production and storage vessel (FPU).
The vessel is currently in the UIE yard in Scotland.
"We will probably not be able to meet current plans of a start up in September," Paul Paulsen, Esso information manager for exploration and production, told Reuters.
"It is taking longer than thought to rectify work done (before) in the Singapore yard and for the instalments necessary to adapt the ship for the Balder field."
Paulsen said the company hoped to have a fresh schedule and new estimates for costs in July or August.
Balder, with recoverable reserves estimated at 170 million barrels, is expected to add 75,000 barrels per day to Norwegian production at peak output.
The field is being developed using subsea wells tied into the FPU, it is the first dedicated installation of this type on the Norwegian continental shelf.
Crude will be offloaded from the production vessel and transported to market by shuttle tankers.
Esso is operator of the development and holds 100 percent equity in block 25/11.
